title: Add Invoice — request form with saved contacts
what: The VCC's Add Deposit button is now Add Invoice: a full request form (deposit #, amount, send-to, CC, 35-character description) that emails the details to billing@unbridledmedia.com and records the request. Send To autofills from every client contact the platform has ever seen, and new name/email pairs are saved automatically for future invoices. Who to CC is a contact search with an + Add New option — each address becomes a removable pill. The billing email is a configurable automation (Invoice Request to Billing) in the admin Automations dashboard.
where: ProFi → open a project → VCC → Client Deposits → + Add Invoice
how: Open the project's VCC tab and click + Add Invoice in the Client Deposits tile.
Fill Deposit # and Amount.
Start typing in Send To — Name: pick a contact to autofill their email, or type a new name and email (saved for next time).
In Who to CC, search contacts and click to add, or type a new email and hit + Add New — addresses stack as pills with ✕ to remove.
Add the invoice description (35 characters max) and submit — billing@unbridledmedia.com gets the request email and the deposit line appears with the invoice number clickable to review.
Track every request in Reports → Client Invoice Report → Requests view.

title: Invoice Request to Billing — email automation
what: Submitting + Add Invoice in the VCC fires a branded request email to accounting with the deposit #, amount, the invoice's send-to and CC, the 35-character description, and who asked. It's now a managed automation in the admin Automations dashboard: the From and To addresses are editable (default billing@unbridledmedia.com) and the email design can be previewed. There is deliberately no CC field on the automation — the invoice's CC list travels inside the email body for accounting to use on the formal invoice.
where: Hub → Admin → Automations ▸ → Invoice Request to Billing
how: Open the Hub as an admin and click Admin, then Automations ▸.
Find Invoice Request to Billing in the list.
Edit From or To if the request should route somewhere else, and Save.
Click Preview to see exactly what accounting receives.
Every + Add Invoice submission from any project's VCC then emails that address automatically (once SMTP is connected).

title: Client Outstanding Invoice Report
what: One report tracking client invoice requests. The default Unsent view lists every invoice that has been requested from a project's VCC but not yet sent — status pill, project, budget owner, deposit #, description, send-to and CC, amount, and who requested it when — with a running unsent total in the header. The All Requests view adds the full history with ✓ Sent / Unsent status on each.
where: Reports → Client Outstanding Invoice Report
how: Open Reports from the Hub and click Client Outstanding Invoice Report.
The Unsent view loads first: everything requested but not yet sent, newest first, with the unsent count and dollar total up top.
Switch to All Requests for the full history including sent invoices and their sent dates.
Click any row to jump to that project in ProFi.

title: Project Estimate PDF
what: A client-ready Project Estimate generated straight from the budget on the Unbridled template. It auto-fills the summary block (client, project title, total, today as the sent date, a valid-through date 30 days out, and who prepared it) and rolls every budget line into the template's four investment buckets: scripting/storyboarding plus the coordination fee land in Pre-Production/Creative; shoots, photography, virtual recording, and misc in Production; the post section in Post-Production; and every travel line in Travel. The bottom line always equals the budget's grand total. It opens as a print-ready page with the print dialog popped — save as PDF or print — with no browser headers or footers on the output.
where: ProFi → open a project → Client Budget → Project Estimate PDF
how: Open the project's budget in ProFi and click Client Budget (top right).
Choose Project Estimate PDF in the pop-out.
A print-ready estimate opens in a new tab with the print dialog ready — pick Save as PDF (or a printer).
Check the four bucket subtotals; the total matches the live budget, so update the budget and regenerate if numbers move.

title: Share Budget Options
what: One pop-out for every client-facing view of the budget, opened from the Share Budget Options button on the Finance page. It gathers the Budget Overview, three share views — Itemized with Cost (the full line-by-line budget), Itemized — Subtotals Only (every line item and quantity, with dollars only at section subtotal and total level), and Non-Itemized — Subtotals Only (rolled-up section subtotals, no line detail) — plus the Project Estimate PDF. The last-used share view is remembered, and picking one opens the shareable client page in a new tab.
where: ProFi → open a project's budget → Share Budget Options (top right)
how: Open the project's budget in ProFi and click Share Budget Options.
Pick how the client should see it: Budget Overview, Itemized with Cost, Itemized — Subtotals Only, or Non-Itemized — Subtotals Only.
The client page opens in a new tab — copy its link to send; the choice is saved as the budget's share mode.
Use Project Estimate PDF from the same pop-out for the print-ready estimate document.

title: Checklists — custom groups, items, and deletes
what: Each of the four Logistics checklists (Recap, Interviews/B-Roll, Commercial/Creative, What to Bring to Set) can now be shaped per project: add your own groups, add items into any group (built-in or custom), and delete any row with the ✕ at its right. Customizations save to your browser per project, just like the checkmarks, and the progress counts include them.
where: FreePro → open a shoot → Logistics → Producer Checklist
how: Open a checklist from the row of pills at the top of the Producer Checklist tab.
Click + Add Group, type a name, and hit Add — the new section appears at the bottom.
Click + Add Item, pick which group it belongs to, type the item, and Add.
Delete any row — built-in or custom — with the ✕ at its right (with a confirm).
Assignments (the person icon) and checkmarks work the same on custom items.

title: Per-shoot Gear tab — Person Responsible + DIT drives
what: The shoot's Gear Management tab now leads with who owns the gear: the Person Responsible for Gear picker sits at the top, with a DIT — Drives tile directly beneath it for tagging hard drives to this shoot. + Tag Drive opens a searchable picker (name, tag, serial, or location); tagging a drive that's on another shoot warns before moving it, and returned drives go back to their home location. Everything feeds the Hard Drives report. Storage Location, Online Rentals, and Rental House info follow below.
where: FreePro → open a shoot → Gear → Gear Management
how: Open the shoot's Gear tab — Person Responsible for Gear is the first tile; pick the crew member who owns gear for this shoot.
In DIT — Drives, click + Tag Drive and search by drive name, asset tag, serial, or location.
Click a drive to tag it to this shoot (a warning appears if it's currently on another shoot).
Click Return on a drive when it comes back — it shows in the office again on the Hard Drives report.

title: Talent call times feed the Schedule
what: Individual talent call times now live on the schedule instead of a column on the crew sheet. Each talent's per-day call time — set in their Add/Edit Talent form under Call Times by Day, now with a call location field beside each time — appears on that day's Schedule timeline as its own 'Talent Call — [name]' entry with a Talent tag, their role, and a 📍 location. The same call time and location show on the talent's shared call sheet under the day header.
where: FreePro → open a shoot → Crew → talent's Edit form → Call Times by Day (shows on Logistics → Schedule)
how: Open the shoot's Crew tab and click Edit on a talent row (or + Add Talent).
Under Call Times by Day, set the time and type the call location for each shoot day they're needed.
Save — the Schedule timeline for that day now shows 'Talent Call — [name]' at the right slot with the location.
The talent's shared call sheet shows their call time and location in the day header.

title: Hard drive tracking + Hard Drives report
what: Every hard drive in the asset database (HDD category) now has a live location. Tag drives onto a shoot from the shoot's Gear tab DIT — Drives tile (or its gear dashboard); return them when they come home. The Hard Drives report is the roster: every drive with where it is right now — ✈ out on a shoot (with the shoot code and who tagged it, since when) or 🏠 home at its office location — filterable to All / On Shoots / In Office and searchable by name, tag, serial, or location.
where: Reports → Hard Drives (tagging happens on each shoot's Gear tab)
how: Open Reports → Hard Drives to see the full roster and each drive's current location.
Filter with the All / On Shoots / In Office pills or search by name, tag, serial, or location.
Click a row on an out drive to jump to the shoot holding it.
To tag or return a drive, use the DIT — Drives tile on a shoot's Gear tab: + Tag Drive to send it out, Return when it's back.

title: Gear request availability — reservations subtracted
what: The equipment picker in the gear request form now shows what's actually available for your dates, not just what exists. Each model's count is the assets marked available in Asset Management minus the quantity sourced 'Internal' on any other shoot whose dates overlap yours — shown as e.g. '6 of 10 available · 4 on other shoots' with the reserved note in yellow (red at zero). Counts refresh if you switch the project on the form; shoots without dates are treated conservatively.
where: Gear Report → + New Gear Request → any department's + Add Gear picker (also on a shoot's Gear Request tab)
how: Open a gear request and pick the project — the inventory counts key off that shoot's dates.
Open a department's + Add Gear picker: each model shows 'X of Y available' after subtracting internal reservations on overlapping shoots.
A yellow 'N on other shoots' note shows how many are spoken for; zero available turns red.
Set quantities as usual — the counts are informational, so you can still request more and sort sourcing on the Gear List.

title: Gear Report — the Gear Manager's home base
what: The Gear Report absorbed the old FreePro Gear Management page (that toggle is gone). One page now has it all: a shoot timeline (gantt) capped at five rows with vertical scroll and pinned date headers, and the full shoot table — Countdown, code, name, Person Responsible, dates, Travel, gear request status (greyed shoots haven't requested), request name, the green (!) needs-assignment flag, and the four gear-source columns with the printable internal check-out list. + New Gear Request and the Asset Management database live in the header. Rows open the shoot's gear dashboard; a green ✓ quick-views the submitted request.
where: Reports → Gear Report
how: Open Reports → Gear Report — the timeline shows upcoming shoots (scroll vertically for more than five, horizontally through dates).
Scan the table: greyed rows still need a gear request; the green (!) means gear awaits source assignment.
Click + New Gear Request to submit one, or Asset Management to open the equipment database.
Click a row for the shoot's gear dashboard, a green ✓ to quick-view its request, or the print icon for the internal check-out list.

title: Creative Assets (AvocadoPost)
what: A Creative Assets tab next to each project's Video Tracker: drag photos, motion graphics, or any files anywhere onto the panel (or multi-select via + Upload Asset, 20MB each). It's a list view — file name (click to download), size, uploader, and date — and every asset can be tagged to one or more videos from the tracker. Tags show as chips with ✕ to untag, a 'Tag new uploads to' selector pre-tags drops, and every tag or upload logs a note in that video's activity feed so its history shows what arrived and when.
where: AvocadoPost → open a project page → Creative Assets tab
how: Open the project page in AvocadoPost and click Creative Assets (next to Project Video Tracker).
Drag files onto the panel, or click + Upload Asset — optionally set 'Tag new uploads to' first so drops land pre-tagged.
Tag any asset to more videos with its + tag… dropdown; click a chip's ✕ to untag one video.
Each tag/upload writes a note into that video's activity; click a file name to download it.

title: Travel — Driving with schedule tiles
what: A Driving section on the Travel tab (below Rental Cars) for crew driving to a shoot. + Driver opens a form with the driver (crew dropdown), tap-to-tag passengers, required From and To cities with live map-validated autocomplete (type 'Columbia MO' or 'Columbia, Missouri' — both work; unmappable entries are flagged in red), a required departure date and time, car make/model, and notes. Saving computes an estimated drive time from the route and feeds two tiles onto the Schedule timeline: 🚗 Drive Departure at the departure time (with the ~drive-time badge, route, car, and passengers) and 🚗 Approx. Drive Arrival at departure-plus-drive-time.
where: FreePro → open a shoot → Logistics → Travel → Driving → + Driver
how: On the Travel tab, click + Driver under the Driving section.
Pick the driver, tap teammates to tag them as passengers.
Type the From and To cities and pick from the live suggestions (state codes or full names both match); set the departure date and time; add the car make/model.
Save — the drive shows on Travel with the estimated drive time, and the Schedule timeline gets Drive Departure and Approx. Drive Arrival tiles for the right day(s).

title: Music Resources — team music library with tags
what: A shared library of music links — licensing platforms, go-to tracks, playlists — that anyone on the team can add to. Links are grouped by tags (Recap, Corporate Talking Head, Documentary, Show Opener, and more), and tag chips under the search bar filter the list to one group. New tags can be added by anyone; duplicates are blocked automatically. A search bar covers names, tags, notes, and links.
where: Reports & Resources → Music Resources
how: Open Reports & Resources from the hub and click the Music Resources tile.
Click a tag chip (e.g. Recap) to filter to that group; click it again to show all.
Click + Add Resource, enter the title and link, pick a Tag from the dropdown (or choose + Add new tag…), and add optional notes.
Use + Add tag next to the chips to create a new tag for everyone — duplicate names are rejected.
Click any link title to open it in a new tab; ✕ removes an entry.

title: Video References — inspiration library with tags
what: A companion library for reference and inspiration videos — style frames, past work, and examples to point clients at. It shares the same tag list as Music Resources, so the groups (Recap, Documentary, Concert Sizzle, Training Videos, etc.) stay consistent across both libraries. Filter with the tag chips, search across everything, and add new tags as the catalog grows.
where: Reports & Resources → Video References
how: Open Reports & Resources from the hub and click the Video References tile.
Click + Add Resource, paste the video link, give it a title, and pick a Tag so it lands in the right group.
Click a tag chip to see only that group — handy when pulling references for a specific video type.
Add notes like what the reference is good for (pacing, framing, look) so teammates know why it's saved.

title: Vendor Contracts Report — every contractor, one page
what: One report of every contractor being hired across production and post: crew contractor slots plus Color and Audio contractors from each project's Video Tracker. Rows are ordered by start date with Start/End columns, estimated totals, and a contract status pill (Signed / Sent / Not sent). Clicking a row opens the contract's details — rates, dates, total, scope of work, signature status — with links to the signing page and the source (Crew tab or AvocadoPost). Slots archive automatically once their end date passes, tucked behind an Archived toggle.
where: Reports & Resources → Vendor Contracts
how: Open Reports & Resources from the hub and click Vendor Contracts.
Scan the list — active slots sort by start date; the header counts how many still have no contract sent.
Click any row to open the detail pop-out: contractor, dates, cost breakdown, scope, and signature status.
From the pop-out, open the signing page or jump to the project's Crew tab / AvocadoPost tracker to send or fix the contract.
Use 'Only not sent' to chase missing contracts, and 'Archived (N)' to review slots whose end date has passed.

title: Color & Audio tracker — post contractors on the Video Tracker
what: Each AvocadoPost project page gets a Color & Audio table under the Video Tracker. + Add Color / + Add Audio open a form with roster name search (auto-fills their email), rate, services, start/end dates, total estimate, and Send Final Invoice To (defaults to you). Click any row to reopen the form; Hold Cost → VCC posts the total to the project VCC under Labor, and every named contractor feeds the Vendor Contracts report automatically.
where: AvocadoPost → open a project page → Project Video Tracker tab → Color & Audio
how: Open the project's page in AvocadoPost and scroll below the Video Tracker.
Click + Add Color or + Add Audio; start typing a name to search the roster, or type a new contractor.
Fill rate, services, dates, and the total estimate; pick who gets the final invoice.
Click a row anytime to reopen the form; use Hold Cost → VCC to hold the total on the budget (coded to Labor).
The contractor now shows on Reports & Resources → Vendor Contracts with dates and status.

title: Send Contract — post-production contractors
what: Contract Editor tiles and Color/Audio rows can now send a signable contract, same flow as crew contracts. Send Contract generates the agreement from what's on screen and opens a review pop-out — recipient, working dates, quoted total, scope of work, invoice-to, new-vendor note — then emails it from info@unbridledmedia.com with a signing link. The signing page shows the flat quoted total, and signatures flow back to the Vendor Contracts report.
where: AvocadoPost → edit page (Contract Editor tile) or Project Video Tracker → Color & Audio row
how: Fill in the contractor's name, email, rate/services, and total.
Click Send Contract — the agreement is generated and the review pop-out opens prefilled.
Adjust anything (dates, total, scope), then Send Contract Email — or Copy Signing Link to send it yourself.
The contractor opens the link, reviews, and types their name to sign; status updates to Signed on the Vendor Contracts report.

title: Room/Space quick-fill on schedule events
what: Every Room/Space you've entered on a shoot's schedule is remembered for that shoot and offered back as one-click chips (and typing suggestions) under the field on both the add and edit event forms — so 'Ballroom 3' only ever gets typed once per show.
where: FreePro → Schedule → + Add Event / edit an event → Room / Space
how: Add an event and type a room into Room / Space — it's saved with the event.
On the next event, the saved rooms appear as chips under the field; click one to fill it.
Typing also suggests matches from the shoot's saved rooms.

title: Travel forms pull the full roster
what: Crew dropdowns across the Travel tab — flights, hotel confirmations, rental cars, and drivers — now offer everyone: people assigned to the shoot first (with their position), then the full company roster. Travel can be booked before the crew list is final. Rental car pickup/dropoff fields also live-search real places so the location carries a mappable address into the Locations tab.
where: FreePro → Travel → any Add Flight / Add Confirmation / Add Rental Car / Add Driver form
how: Open any travel form and click the crew dropdown — 'On this shoot' lists assigned crew, 'Full roster' lists everyone else.
Picking a person auto-fills their name on the booking.
For rental cars, type the pickup spot and pick a suggestion — the resolved address feeds the Locations tab.
Flights also have a Duplicate button to book the same flight for another crew member, confirming just their cost and confirmation #.

title: Schedule tiles — addresses right, drive times built in
what: Event tiles on the internal schedule and all shared views (producer, crew, client) put the location's address on the right side of the tile, with an estimated drive time from the previous stop directly under it. The drive chain covers located events, one-off locations, and reservation meals — so a full shoot day reads like a route.
where: FreePro → Schedule, and every shared schedule view
how: Give events locations (saved or one-off) — the address shows right-aligned on the tile.
When consecutive events are at different addresses, '🚗 X min from prev' appears under the address automatically.
The same layout and drive times appear on producer, crew, and client links.

title: Catering — Delivery checkbox & reservations as driving stops
what: Catering forms get a Delivery checkbox (top right) and the time field is now Reservation/Delivery Time. Checked = the food comes to you, exactly as before. Unchecked = it's a reservation: the meal tile gets a Reservation badge, the restaurant's address joins the day's driving chain with its own drive time, and the next event calculates its drive from the restaurant.
where: FreePro → Schedule → + Catering/Meals (or the Catering/Meals page)
how: Add or edit a meal; leave Delivery checked for drop-offs.
Uncheck Delivery for a restaurant reservation and enter the address and reservation time.
The schedule shows the meal with a Reservation badge and 🚗 drive times in and out of the stop — internally and on shared views.

title: One-off event locations with live place search
what: Event forms take a one-off location without touching the Locations tab: an '…or type a one-off location' field under the Location dropdown live-searches real places. Picking a result attaches the mappable address — it shows on the tile and joins the drive-time chain — while staying off the project's Locations list. Freehand text works too (label only).
where: FreePro → Schedule → + Add Event / edit an event → Location
how: Leave the Location dropdown on — No location —.
Type the place into the one-off field and pick a suggestion; a green ✓ shows the resolved address.
The event tile shows the 📍 name with the address on the right and drive times to/from it.
Picking a saved location from the dropdown clears the one-off.

title: Jump to Live + pulsing live events
what: On producer, crew, and client links, any event whose time block is happening right now pulses an orange left edge — and a Jump to Live button (with a matching pulsing dot) sits under Jump to Schedule. It scrolls straight to the live event, or the one that started within the last hour, or the next one coming up, centered on screen. Events light up and clear on their own as the day moves.
where: Any producer, crew, or client share link
how: Open a share link on a shoot day — the current time block pulses orange.
Tap Jump to Live to land on what's happening right now.
Lunch and reservation meals pulse during their windows too.

title: Swipe left for phone reminders
what: On a phone, swipe any timeline tile left in producer, crew, or client view to reveal an orange +Reminder button. Tapping it opens the phone's calendar pre-filled with the item's title, time, and location, plus a 30-minutes-before alert — one tap to save and your phone pings you before the event. Works on schedule events, call/lunch/wrap, catering, and flights (flights use the real departure time, timezone-safe). A small “swipe left to add reminders” hint sits next to the Schedule header.
where: Any producer, crew, or client share link on a phone
how: Open a share link on your phone and scroll to the Schedule.
Swipe a tile to the left — the +Reminder button appears.
Tap it, then save the pre-filled event in your calendar; it alerts 30 minutes before.

title: Live pulse everywhere — internal schedule + in-air flights
what: The pulsing orange live edge now runs everywhere, not just on share links. The internal Schedule tab pulses the current time block as you work, and flight tiles pulse while the plane is actually in the air — from departure until arrival, using the flight's real timestamps so timezones can't fool it. The pulse clears on its own when the block ends, the flight lands, or its live status flips to Arrived.
where: Project → Schedule, plus producer, crew, and client share links
how: Open the Schedule tab (or any share link) during a shoot day — the block happening right now pulses orange.
Flights pulse for the whole time they're in the air, then stop at landing.
Nothing to configure — tiles light up and clear automatically as the day moves.

title: Email Outbox — see and delete automation emails
what: The admin Automations dashboard now has an Outbox tab that records every email the automations produce. Once Outlook is connected each one is logged as Sent or Failed (with the error if it bounced); while email is still off, the same emails are captured as Drafts so you can see exactly what's queued to go out. Filter by All, Drafts, Sent, or Failed (each with a live count), click any row to preview the real rendered email, and delete drafts you don't want sent. Sent and failed history is kept — only drafts can be deleted.
where: The Hub → ⚙ Admin → Automations → Outbox tab (admin only)
how: On the Hub, open ⚙ Admin at the bottom, then click Automations.
Switch to the Outbox tab and use the All / Drafts / Sent / Failed chips to filter.
Click View on any row to preview the full email, or Delete on a draft to stop it from going out.

title: Color-code rows on the Video Tracker
what: Every row on a project's Video Tracker can be given a color for quick visual grouping. Hover the pencil at the start of a row and a palette of 10 colors appears; pick one and the whole row tints to that color. It's per-deliverable and sticks, so you can flag priorities, group related videos, or mark status at a glance. Clicking the pencil still opens the edit as before.
where: AvocadoPost → a project page → Project Video Tracker tab
how: Open a project in AvocadoPost and go to the Project Video Tracker tab.
Hover the pencil (✎) at the left of any row to reveal the 10-color palette.
Click a color to tint the row, or Clear to remove it.

title: Multiple of the same position, auto-numbered
what: You can now add more than one of the same crew position to a project — a second On-Site Editor, a third Camera Operator, and so on. When a position appears more than once, the crew grid numbers them automatically (On-Site Editor 1, On-Site Editor 2…), and those numbers carry through to the call sheets and share views so everyone can tell the roles apart. A position that appears only once stays unnumbered.
where: FreePro → Logistics → Crew → + Add Position
how: On the Crew tab, click + Add Position and pick a position that's already on the project.
Add it — the grid labels the duplicates 1, 2, 3… in order.
The numbering shows on the crew roster, call sheets, and share links automatically.

title: Duplicate a row on the Project Video Tracker
what: Every row on the Project Video Tracker now has a duplicate button next to its edit pencil. Click it to instantly create a copy of that deliverable — same type, category, specs, timeline, and assignments — as a new row right below, so you can spin up near-identical edits without re-entering everything.
where: AvocadoPost → open a project → Project Video Tracker → the ⧉ button beside each row’s pencil
how: Open a project page and go to the Project Video Tracker tab.
Find the row you want to copy and click the ⧉ duplicate button next to its pencil.
A copy titled “… (copy)” appears directly below — rename or tweak it as needed.

title: Creative on an edit — RFR notifies the PM and the Creative
what: Each edit now has a Creative field beside Project Manager, chosen from the creative team (with an Add New option). When someone clicks RFR (Ready For Review), the notification goes to both the Project Manager and the Creative, so the right people are looped in on every review.
where: AvocadoPost → open an edit → Details → Creative (next to Project Manager)
how: Open an edit from the pipeline or the Project Video Tracker.
In Details, use the Creative dropdown next to Project Manager to pick the creative (or choose + Add New).
When you click RFR, both the Project Manager and the Creative are notified.

title: Light view — switch the whole platform to a light theme
what: A Light view / Dark view toggle sits at the bottom of every signed-in page. Click it to flip the entire platform between the default dark theme and a bright, print-friendly light theme. Your choice is remembered on this device and applied everywhere — the Hub, projects, ProFi, AvocadoPost, and reports.
where: Any signed-in page → bottom center → Light view / Dark view button
how: Scroll to the bottom of any page while signed in.
Click 'Light view' to switch to the light theme (the button then reads 'Dark view').
Click it again to switch back; the platform remembers your preference on this device.

title: Post-Production Overview — version stepper & Approve
what: The Post-Production Overview table now lets you drive each deliverable's version and sign-off right from the row. A -1 / V x.x / +1 stepper bumps the version number as new cuts go out, and an Approve button marks the edit approved (it flips to a green '✓ Approved'). RFR and Sent to Client stay one click away, so the whole review loop lives on one screen.
where: AvocadoPost → open a project page → Post-Production Overview
how: Open a project in AvocadoPost; the Post-Production Overview is the first tab.
Use -1 / +1 next to the version number to step an edit's version up or down.
Click Approve when a cut is signed off — it turns into '✓ Approved'.
RFR and Sent to Client buttons sit in the same row for the rest of the review loop.

title: Project Video Tracker — fully customizable columns & cells
what: The Project Video Tracker is now a spreadsheet you control. Add your own columns (+ Add Column) for anything the team tracks, and show, hide, or remove columns from the ⚙ menu. Resize a column by dragging its edge, sort or filter from the icons in each header, and drag rows by the handle to reorder. Merge Cells joins adjacent cells so one value can span a group, and every cell — Type, Category, Notes, Video Assets, and any custom column — is editable inline. Title, due date, editor, review link, and status still feed live from each edit, so the grid stays in sync while the extra columns are yours to shape.
where: AvocadoPost → open a project page → Project Video Tracker
how: Open a project in AvocadoPost and go to the Project Video Tracker tab.
Click + Add Column to create a custom column; use the ⚙ menu to show, hide, or remove columns.
Drag a column's edge to resize it; use the sort/filter icons in a header to reorder or narrow rows.
Drag the handle at the left of a row to move it; select cells and click Merge Cells to span a value.
Click any cell to edit it inline — custom columns and Type/Notes/Video Assets save as you go.

title: Add Deliverable — full field parity with the edit card
what: The Add Deliverable form now carries every field the AvocadoPost edit card has — Video Title, Description, Status, Type, Category, Lead Editor, Project Manager, Creative, Aspect Ratio, Resolution, Frame Rate, Drive, Asset Ref, Music Ref, Start/Due dates, and Review Link. Whatever you set when creating a deliverable flows straight into the editing pipeline (and edits made there flow back), so nothing has to be re-entered later.
where: FreePro → open a project → Deliverable tab → + Add Deliverable
how: Open a project in FreePro and go to the Deliverable tab.
Click + Add Deliverable to open the form.
Fill any of the fields — including Creative, Frame Rate, and Drive — then save.
The new deliverable appears in the AvocadoPost pipeline with everything you entered.

title: Dark Day — a new Key Date type
what: Key Dates now include a 'Dark Day' option alongside Shoot Day and the other day types, so travel days, prep days, or rest days between shoots can be labeled clearly on the project timeline.
where: FreePro → open a project → Overview → Key Dates
how: Open a project in FreePro; Key Dates are on the Overview tab.
Click the day-type pill next to a date.
Choose 'Dark Day' from the list.

title: Copy Link on the review link — one click to share
what: When an edit has a Current Review Link, a Copy Link button now sits right beside Open. Copy Link puts the review URL on your clipboard (and confirms with '✓ Copied') so you can paste it into an email or message without opening it first; Open still launches the link in a new tab.
where: AvocadoPost → open an edit → Current Review Link
how: Open an edit in AvocadoPost and find the Current Review Link field.
Click ⧉ Copy Link to copy the URL — it briefly shows '✓ Copied'.
Or click ▶ Open to launch the link in a new tab.

title: VCC PDF — a finance-ready cover summary
what: The VCC now exports a clean PDF from the button beside Vendor Invoices. It opens with a cover Summary Page — Profit Summary and Client Deposits up top, a full-width Reconciliation Calculator below, and per-shoot reconciliation tiles — then the full cost detail follows. It's built for sending straight to finance or a client.
where: ProFi → Reports → VCC → open a project → PDF (left of Vendor Invoices)
how: Open a project's VCC (Reports → VCC → pick a project).
Click the PDF button, just left of Vendor Invoices.
Save or print the generated document — the Summary Page comes first, detail after.

title: Reconciliation Calculator — variance at a glance
what: A Reconciliation Calculator on the VCC ties posted and unposted costs together. Enter the Current ODC Amount (posted charges from accounting); it adds your Current Unposted holds for a Reconciled Total, compares that to Total Direct Costs, and shows the Variance. When the variance hits $0 the field glows green, so you know the VCC is fully reconciled at a glance.
where: ProFi → Reports → VCC → open a project → Reconciliation Calculator
how: Open a project's VCC.
Type the Current ODC Amount from your accounting/ODC report.
Watch the Reconciled Total and Variance update; a $0 variance glows green when everything ties out.

title: Total by Category on the VCC
what: The old 'Breakage by Category' box is now 'Total by Category', moved up to where the shoot total used to sit, with any per-shoot totals lined up to its right. It sums every direct cost by budget category so you can see where the money is going without scrolling the full ledger.
where: ProFi → Reports → VCC → open a project → Total by Category
how: Open a project's VCC.
Read the Total by Category box for a per-category roll-up of all direct costs.
Per-shoot totals sit to its right when the project has multiple shoots.

title: Harbinger — guided project-initiation wizard
what: The Harbinger kickoff is now a step-by-step wizard instead of one long form. Six stages run across a liquid-glass icon dock at the top — Project, Client, Revenue/Commissions, Creative, Production/Crew, Key Dates — matching the app's bottom navs; the active stage highlights orange and completed stages glow green. A left panel shows one dot per field on the current stage: gray until filled, orange once filled (required or not), red if a required field is skipped. Move freely with the tabs or the green Next arrow — the page slides and the active icon pops on each move. Final review is gated until every required field is filled; the pulsing "Submit Harbinger & Go Live" button only appears on the condensed review page. Stage upgrades: Client is now an + Add Client Info pop-out that builds contact tiles with Primary and Invoice POC badges (a Primary and an Invoice POC are required); Revenue auto-calculates Total Budget from Media Budget + CapCo Revenue and hides commission fields behind a Commissionable Project toggle; Creative condenses the direction notes and collects video references as tag bubbles; Production has a No Shoot toggle (auto-selected when the budget has no production items) that grays the shoot logistics, with searchable Preferred PM/Producer/Crew/Editors.
where: ProFi → open a project → Finance → Submit Harbinger (fires when a budget moves to Live)
how: Open a project's budget in ProFi and start the Harbinger (Submit Harbinger, or when moving the budget Live).
Work through the six tabs at the top — the left dots show what's filled (orange), skipped-and-required (red), or still empty (gray).
On Client, click + Add Client Info to add each contact, then mark one Primary and one Invoice POC.
On Revenue, enter Media Budget and any CapCo Revenue — Total Budget calculates itself; flip Commissionable Project on to add commission owners and %.
On Production, toggle No Shoot if there is no shoot (it self-selects when the budget has none); add searchable Preferred PM/Producer/Crew/Editors.
Advance with the green Next arrow or the tabs; once every required field is filled, click Review Harbinger, then the pulsing Submit Harbinger & Go Live.

title: Budget versions — new-version prompt on open
what: Opening a project's budget now offers to start a new version. A prompt lists every version of that budget — the current one plus any frozen snapshots — each with its full grand total and the date and time it was last opened, so you can see at a glance how the number has moved across revisions. Continue keeps you on the current version; starting a new version saves the current budget as a read-only snapshot and rolls the version number forward.
where: ProFi → open a project → Budget
how: Open any project's budget in ProFi.
Read the prompt — each row shows a version, its total budget, and when it was last opened.
Click Continue on V# to keep editing the current version,
or click + Start Version # to freeze the current budget as a snapshot and begin a fresh version.

title: Mobile budget — collapsible header card
what: On phones the budget's header card (Budget Dated, Solutions Code, Budget Owner, Est. Final Delivery, Close Month, Client Contact, Tagged, and Total) used to stack into a tall block that filled the screen. It now collapses to a compact bar showing the Total Budget and the status pill, with a Details toggle. Tap Details to expand the full editable field grid; tap Hide to collapse it again. Desktop is unchanged.
where: ProFi → open a project → Budget (on a phone)
how: Open a project's budget on a phone.
The header shows a compact Total Budget + status bar by default.
Tap Details to expand the full fields (dates, owner, client contact, and so on).
Tap Hide to collapse back to the compact bar.

title: Mobile budget — condensed line items with a detail popout
what: On phones each budget line is condensed to three columns — the scope/item name, a + button, and the line total — so the budget no longer scrolls sideways. Tapping the + opens a popout with the rest of that line's detail: notes, hrs/days, unit cost, the live subtotal, and Duplicate / Delete. Everything stays fully editable. Desktop keeps its full multi-column table.
where: ProFi → open a project → Budget (on a phone)
how: Open a project's budget on a phone.
Each line shows just the item name, a + button, and the line total.
Tap the + on a line to open its details (notes, hrs/days, unit cost, subtotal).
Edit any field there, or use Duplicate / Delete, then close to return to the list.

title: Dashboard — animated reveal on open
what: The Dashboard now animates as it loads. The Media Moment, Day in Review, My Tasks, and Team Today tiles drop in from the top in a light cascade, and the Project Hub tile flies in from the side with a fade. The motion respects the system 'reduce motion' accessibility setting.
where: The Hub (Dashboard) — on load
how: Open the Dashboard.
The top tiles drop in from above and the hub tile flies in — no action needed.

title: Project ⇄ Client Hub — one flip tile
what: The Dashboard's Project Hub and Client Hub are now a single always-open tile that flips between the two. A search box and the green New Project button sit at the top-left; an icon switch button on the right flips the tile — Switch to Client Hub, then back to Project Hub. On each switch the cards flip in one by one from the left and the accent retints (orange for projects, gray for clients). The project row and client row each scroll sideways through everything.
where: The Hub (Dashboard) → Project Hub tile
how: On the Dashboard, use the search box in the hub tile to find a project (or client).
Scroll the card row sideways to browse.
Click the switch button on the right (Switch to Client Hub / Project Hub) to flip between the two hubs.
Use the green + (New Project) on the left to start a project.

title: Hub tile app menu — jump to Finance, Production, Post
what: The Project Hub tile has an orange menu (three-line) button on the right. Clicking it expands three icon shortcuts — Project Finance, Production, and Post Production — that take you straight to those apps. Each shows its name on hover, matching the + and switch buttons.
where: The Hub (Dashboard) → Project Hub tile → menu button
how: On the Dashboard's hub tile, click the orange three-line menu button on the right.
Three app shortcuts expand to its left: Project Finance, Production, Post Production.
Hover any icon to see its name; click to open that app.

title: Bottom nav everywhere — Home, Calendar, Reports, Team
what: The Dashboard's floating bottom navigation now follows you onto the Calendar, Reports, and Team pages, so you can jump between them from anywhere (each option respects your role's permissions). The first button is now Home on every page — it returns you to the Dashboard — replacing the old View switch.
where: Dashboard, Calendar, Reports, and Team pages — bottom nav
how: From the Dashboard, Calendar, Reports, or Team page, use the floating bottom nav.
Tap Home to return to the Dashboard, or Calendar / Reports / Team to jump between them.

title: Dashboard — Day in Review, My Tasks & Team Today as three tiles
what: The lower dashboard is now three separate tiles instead of two stacked cards — Day in Review, My Tasks, and Team Today — each with an orange header. My Tasks has its own tile with quick add and check-off and a 'Task Due Today' flag; Team Today lists who's in the office, traveling, or out. The row is responsive: three across on wide screens, stacking down on smaller ones.
where: The Hub (Dashboard)
how: Open the Dashboard.
Scan Day in Review for today's shoots, due dates, and what's coming tomorrow.
Use My Tasks to add (+ Add New) and check off tasks — a Task Due Today flag appears when relevant.
Check Team Today for who is in office, traveling, or out.

title: Dashboard — cursor-following highlight on the tiles
what: Hovering the dashboard tiles (Project/Client Hub, Day in Review, My Tasks, Team Today) shows a subtle orange highlight that follows the cursor behind the content — a light interactive touch that respects the system reduce-motion setting.
where: The Hub (Dashboard) — hover any tile
how: Move your mouse over any dashboard tile.
A faint orange glow tracks the cursor behind the text.

title: Finance role — Project Hub with per-project Overview & Finance
what: Signed in as Finance, the dashboard now shows the Project Hub — a searchable, scrollable list of every project — instead of a single ProFi tile. The search sits at the left and a $ Project Finance shortcut is pinned to the right. Opening a project lands on a focused view with just two tabs, Overview and Project Finance (the full budget), so finance can go straight from the roster to a project's numbers.
where: The Hub (Dashboard), as the Finance role
how: Sign in as Finance and open the Dashboard.
Search or scroll the Project Hub to find a project.
Click a project to open it on the Overview / Project Finance tabs.
Use the $ button at the top-right of the hub to jump to the full Project Finance list.

title: Crew call-time override — per day, on the schedule
what: Add/Edit Crew now lets you override a crew member's call time for a specific day. Each override drops a "NAME — Call Time" tile onto that day's schedule with an optional location and notes, and it carries all the way through to the producer and crew online views and the Daily Crew Call Sheet PDF.
where: FreePro → project → Logistics → Crew/Talent → Add/Edit a crew member → Call-Time Overrides
how: Open the project, go to Logistics → Crew/Talent, and Add or Edit a crew member.
In the call-time override section every shoot day is listed — type a call time on any day you need to differ from the default.
Optionally set a location and notes for that day's override.
Save — a "NAME — Call Time" tile appears on that day's schedule.
Open the producer/crew share view or the Daily Crew Call Sheet PDF to confirm the override flows through.

title: Talent call sheet email — a ready template per talent
what: Send Call Sheet Emails includes a talent-only template that personalizes the call time, date, location, wardrobe, and point-of-contact for the selected talent. The sign-off uses the field producer's preferred name rather than their full legal name.
where: FreePro → project → Share → Send Call Sheet Emails → Talent
how: Open the project's Send Call Sheet Emails panel.
Choose a talent recipient — the email body auto-fills with that talent's call time, date, and location.
Review the wardrobe note and point-of-contact, which pull from the talent's details.
Send — the talent receives a personalized call sheet email signed by the field producer's preferred name.

title: Person tagging — crew & talent names on every tile
what: Tag individual crew and talent to a schedule event and their names show at the bottom of the event tile — on the internal schedule and on the producer, crew, and talent views. This replaces the old Video/Photo tag chips with the actual people involved.
where: FreePro → project → Schedule → Add/Edit Event → Crew/Talent Tags
how: Open the Schedule and Add or Edit an event.
Under Crew/Talent Tags, pick the crew members and talent involved in that event.
Save — their names appear as pills at the bottom of the tile.
The same names carry through to the producer, crew, and talent share views.

title: Schedule color coding — by category
what: Timeline tiles are color-coded by category — Filming, Meals, Travel, Talent, and General. The colors are customizable in the Color Coding key and apply consistently across the internal schedule and the producer/crew/talent share views.
where: FreePro → project → Schedule → settings gear → Color Coding
how: Open the Schedule and hover/tap the settings gear, then choose Color Coding.
See each category (Filming, Meals, Travel, Talent, General) with its color swatch.
Click a swatch to change that category's color.
Tiles on the schedule and every share view update to match.

title: Event Tag — set a tile's color, add your own
what: Give a single event its own color (Event Tag) that sets the whole tile's color everywhere it appears. You can add your own custom colors to the Color Coding key. The Event Tag picker sits behind an expander on the event form so it stays out of the way until you need it.
where: FreePro → project → Schedule → Add/Edit Event → Event Tag
how: Open the Schedule and Add or Edit an event.
Tap Event Tag to expand the color options (it shows the current pick when collapsed).
Choose a color — or add a new one via + Add Color in the settings gear → Color Coding key.
Save — the tile takes that color across the schedule and share views.

title: Group Tags — group events, filter to one
what: Create your own groups (for example Recap, Social, or Interview), each with its own color that paints the right edge of the tile. Manage groups in the Color Coding key, and use the filter (funnel) button to narrow the schedule to just one group's events.
where: FreePro → project → Schedule → Add/Edit Event → Group Tags; filter via the funnel button
how: Open the Schedule and Add or Edit an event.
Under Group Tags, pick a group or + Add Group to create one (name + color).
Save — the tile's right edge shows the group color.
Use the funnel button (left of the gear) to filter the schedule to a single group.

title: Slate on filming events — opt-in
what: When you mark an event as Filming, a Slate toggle appears next to it. Turn it on and the tile shows a Slate button that opens the digital slate for that event; leave it off and there's no slate. Events default to no slate.
where: FreePro → project → Schedule → Add/Edit Event → Filming → Slate
how: Open the Schedule and Add or Edit an event.
Turn on Filming — a Slate toggle appears beside it.
Turn on Slate if this event should carry a slate.
Save — the tile shows a Slate button; open it to fill the slate. If Slate is off, no button appears.

title: Shot list — Est. Start Time and a tidier day header
what: Scene forms have an Est. Start Time input that cascades to later scenes on save. Each day header shows compact Call/Shooting/Lunch/Wrap tiles pulled from the schedule, a scrollable column-picker menu, and the Public toggle plus + Add Scene tucked into the top/bottom-right for a cleaner, single-line look.
where: FreePro → project → Shot List
how: Open the Shot List for a project.
Add or Edit a scene and set its Est. Start Time — later scenes shift on save.
Read the day's Call/Shooting/Lunch/Wrap times in the compact header tiles (fed from the schedule).
Use the column menu to show/hide columns (it scrolls), the Public toggle to share a day, and + Add Scene to add rows.
